Early skin-to-skin contact and neonatal outcomes: a randomized trial

Rokeya Begum | Kamal Ahmed

Abstract

Background: Skin-to-skin contact immediately after birth may improve neonatal outcomes, but trial evidence from low-income settings is limited.

Methods: We randomized 400 term newborns in Dhaka to immediate skin-to-skin contact or standard care.

Results: Hypothermia occurred in 6% versus 19% of newborns.

Conclusions: Immediate skin-to-skin contact sharply reduced neonatal hypothermia.

Key words hypothermia, newborn, randomized trial

5 | CONCLUSIONS

Immediate skin-to-skin contact is a cheap and effective way to prevent hypothermia in term newborns, and it should become routine care in Bangladeshi hospitals.
